audit.whatIsWrong: The page is built on a mechanic that does not apply. Miasma's GROUNDING is named as the matchup-defining threat in breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, report[5].t, whys[2], wants.you[1] and wants.foe[1] — but grounding only disables movement abilities, and Lillia has none. No dash, no leap, nothing. Separately the slots are wrong: the content layer calls Twin Fang her W and the grounding her E.
audit.why: Riot: Miasma is W (24/22/20/18/16s) and slows, grounds and damages; Twin Fang is E on a 0.75s cooldown and heals her for a share of the damage. The mirror recorded the same error from Cassiopeia's side — a Cassiopeia player saving a 24-second Miasma to 'ground' Lillia was holding it for nothing. From your side the cost is worse: you are told to fear the wrong half of the button and never told the half that actually beats you, which is the SLOW landing on a champion whose entire defence is stacked move speed.
audit.corrected: Every grounding claim replaced with the slow, the slots fixed to Twin Fang (E) and Miasma (W), and Twin Fang's 0.75s cooldown stated so the DPS threat is concrete. Also added: Petrifying Gaze only stuns enemies FACING her — turning and running takes the slow instead of the stun, which is the single most useful unstated fact in this matchup.
sources: ownerKit — no dash or movement ability

notes: packet.games is null for this matchup while the brief's own games field says 353; I did not defer it, because the win rate (46.74) is present and the page has real content. If the null is authoritative this one should be re-checked. The expensive fix here is the grounding: six separate strings told the reader that Miasma disables her dashes and leaps. Lillia has neither. The slow on the same button is the real counter to a champion whose defence is stacked move speed, and Petrifying Gaze's facing rule — stun if you face her, slow if your back is turned — was absent everywhere and is worth more than anything else on the page. Twin Fang also heals her off the damage, so Grievous Wounds has a genuine target; report[8] already says 'add anti-heal early into his sustain' and should say hers. The full layer still uses he/his for Cassiopeia throughout.
